summary: Updates several BGP Extended Community registries, replacing the Experimental Use registration procedure in some entries because their use is clearly not experimental and the label is misleading. It updates RFC 7153 and RFC 8955.

plainLanguage.summary: Some labels on a list said experimental when the things were in real use. This fixes the labels.

questions: what is first come first served registration
subtitle: Corrects IANA registry labels for BGP Extended Communities that are in real use

tldr.problem: BGP Extended Community type values 0x80, 0x81, and 0x82 were labeled as reserved for Experimental Use in IANA registries, but in practice they have been used in production protocols for years.
tldr.mechanism: This RFC updates the IANA registries to relabel these type values with the correct registration procedure (First Come First Served) and removes the misleading 'Experimental Use' label from related sub-type registry names.
tldr.outcome: The registries now accurately reflect how these code points are actually being used, reducing confusion for new implementers.

facts.label: Procedure changed from
facts.value: Experimental Use to First Come First Served

today: RFC 9184 corrects the IANA registries for BGP Extended Communities to accurately reflect their real-world use.

sections.title: The Registry Problem
sections.content:
BGP Extended Communities are attributes used in Border Gateway Protocol routing. These attributes are identified by type and sub-type values that IANA maintains in public registries.

Type values 0x80, 0x81, and 0x82 were reserved for Experimental Use, but in practice these exact type values have been used in standardized RFCs (RFC 5575 and RFC 7674, later consolidated in RFC 8955) for real production routing features. The "Experimental Use" label was misleading.
sections.plainLanguage: Imagine a list of tools marked as experimental, but everyone uses them as standard tools. The label doesn't match reality.

sections.title: Registry Changes
sections.content:
This RFC updates the registry entries to change the registration procedure from "Experimental Use" (reserved for testing) to "First Come First Served" (allowing actual use). This procedure makes it clear that these type values are available for organizations to use for their own extensions.

The RFC also updates the titles of the related sub-type registries, removing the "Experimental Use" label from their names while keeping the ability to register new sub-types under these main types.
sections.plainLanguage: Instead of saying these tools are for testing only, the registry now says people and organizations can use them for their own needs.

sections.title: Impact on BGP Implementations
sections.content:
With this corrected registration procedure, implementers and operators now have clear guidance that type values 0x80, 0x81, and 0x82 are available for use in BGP routing. The types have been used in practical applications like Flowspec (RFC 8955) for controlling traffic engineering.

The accurate registry reduces confusion when organizations or vendors want to define their own extensions using these type values, ensuring they follow the correct registration path rather than assuming the experimental designation prevented deployment.
sections.plainLanguage: Now when network operators and software makers want to add new features to BGP routing, the registry clearly tells them these code numbers are theirs to use.
